ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Hatshepsut

code.originalText: Fourteen-week review: A1c, lipids, weight, periodontal therapy, knees, and screening results

text.paragraph: Fourteen-week review: A1c, lipids, weight, periodontal therapy, knees, and screening results. [S]

Ms. Hatshepsut returns fourteen weeks after diabetes was found. She has taken semaglutide 0.5 mg weekly for three weeks, with mild fullness after large meals and no vomiting, with metformin 1000 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg each evening. She finished scaling and root planing six weeks ago; her gums bleed less. Her screening mammogram last week was normal, and the HPV test, the fecal immunochemical test, and the HIV and hepatitis tests were negative. She walks about 120 minutes a week and climbs the stairs at the sites with less knee pain. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-07-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 88.6 kg, BMI 34.6; blood pressure 120/76, pulse 74

Painful swelling of the left lower jaw for four days, after a throbbing toothache for three weeks under a broken lower left molar; low-grade temperature, no trismus, no swelling of the floor of the mouth or neck; dental abscess suspected

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the dental diagnosis the next day. It echoes the dental disease reported on the mummy identified as hers (R, after the index date), without linking to it.
Acute periapical abscess of the lower left first molar (tooth 19), non-restorable, with a localized buccal vestibular swelling and no spread to fascial spaces; drained and extracted
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; no historical claim is made.

Type 2 diabetes found on screening (hemoglobin A1c 7.6% with a random glucose of 212 mg/dL from the same sample), with thirst and waking at night to pass urine; normal kidney function and urine albumin
S — Synthetic screening finding at intake; not linked to the disputed claim of diabetes on the mummy (R).
Obesity, class 2 (BMI 36.3), with type 2 diabetes and knee osteoarthritis; she wants to feel stronger and move more easily
S — Synthetic finding at intake, recorded in person-first language.
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees: pain on stairs and after standing, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus, no effusion; a clinical diagnosis without imaging
S — Synthetic finding at intake; not linked to the osteoarthritis reported on the mummy (R).
Periodontitis, generalized, stage III, grade C (bone loss to the middle third of the roots, two molars lost earlier to gum disease, and A1c above 7% as a grade modifier)
S — Synthetic finding at the dental consultation.

Acute uncomplicated cystitis (dysuria and frequency for two days, urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite, no fever or flank pain); urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes, at goal (E11.65). A1c 6.6%, down from 7.6%, below the goal of 7%, on metformin, semaglutide and the periodontal treatment. No hypoglycemia. [S]
Continue metformin 1000 mg and semaglutide 0.5 mg; stay at 0.5 mg while she is losing weight and tolerating it.
A1c in three months, then every six months once stable.
Endocrinology is not needed while she is at goal.

Obesity, class 2 (E66.812). Weight 88.6 kg, down 4.4 kg (5%) since intake; she is pleased that the stairs are easier. [S]
Strengthening exercise and protein to protect muscle and bone.

Periodontitis after therapy (K05.323). Inflammation settling after scaling and root planing. [S]
Periodontal maintenance every three months with the dental team.

Knee osteoarthritis (M17.0). Less pain with exercise, weight loss and topical diclofenac. [S]
Continue the program; diclofenac gel as needed.

Cardiovascular risk. LDL 76 mg/dL on atorvastatin 20 mg, below 100 mg/dL; ALT normal; no muscle symptoms. [S]
Continue atorvastatin; lipids yearly.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Section 2, Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes; Section 9, Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment) (2026); Obesity and Weight Management for the Prevention and Treatment of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Section 8) (2026); Cardiovascular Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Section 10) (2026); Scientific evidence on the links between periodontal diseases and diabetes: Consensus report and guidelines of the joint workshop on periodontal diseases and diabetes by the International Diabetes Federation and the European Federation of Periodontology (2018); 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and hyperlipidemia monographs (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: Review in three months with A1c; periodontal maintenance every three months; second hepatitis B dose next week; influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in the autumn; next preventive visit in one year. [S]
